Deinfibulation, compared to women with infibulation, is used to prevent and treat complications of type III female genital mutilation (FGM). A retrospective case-control study showed very low-quality evidence, with 43 fewer complications per 1,000 women (confidence interval: 83 fewer to 61 more). The evidence was downgraded due to risk of bias in case and control selection, overlap in confidence intervals, and a small number of participants in the control group. 6. Deinfibulation, compared to women with no FGM, is used to prevent and treat complications of type III FGM. The evidence quality was very low, with 47 more complications per 1,000 women. The evidence was downgraded due to selection bias, statistical heterogeneity, and imprecision in effect estimates. 7. Antepartum deinfibulation versus intrapartum deinfibulation for childbirth in women with type III FGM was assessed. A retrospective observational study and a case-control study provided very low-quality evidence, with 14 fewer complications per 1,000 women (confidence interval: 263 fewer to 175 more). The evidence was downgraded due to selection bias, uncertainty in effect magnitude, and wide overlapping confidence intervals. 8. Providing information to improve body image and care-seeking behavior in women and girls living with FGM was evaluated. The evidence quality was very low, with 119 more women per 1,000 seeking care (confidence interval: 52 more to 205 more). The evidence was downgraded due to selection bias, statistical heterogeneity, and reliance on a single small study. 9. Counseling prior to deinfibulation in women with type III FGM was compared to no counseling. The evidence quality was very low, with 107 fewer complications per 1,000 women (confidence interval: 226 fewer to 122 more). The evidence was downgraded due to selection bias, wide confidence intervals, and a small number of participants from a single study. 10. Providing information about the consequences of FGM to healthcare providers caring for women and girls with FGM was assessed to improve provider attitudes and client satisfaction. The evidence quality was very low, with 154 more women per 1,000 reporting improved satisfaction (confidence interval: 26 fewer to 460 more). The evidence was downgraded due to selection bias, wide confidence intervals, and a small sample size. 11. Clitoral reconstruction for treating female sexual dysfunction in women with FGM was evaluated. The evidence quality was very low, with 400 fewer adverse outcomes per 1,000 women (confidence interval: 30 fewer to 630 fewer). The evidence was downgraded due to selection bias, small sample size, loss to follow-up, use of non-validated scales, and significant statistical heterogeneity. Some studies reported worsened clitoral response postoperatively, while others showed significant improvement in sexual function scores at six months post-surgery.
